maya: FYI - nightly TP run (2B model, 8xA100) shows a regression in step p99 and steady-state throughput, ~12-18% worse vs last week. looks tied to all-reduce behavior. flamegraph attached but quick summary below.

liam: ugh, saw a bump in our dashboards too. any obvious kernel or nccl logs?

maya: pasted the clipped trace from the runtime profiler. main wheel: repeated small-message all-reduces (avg ~9KB per rank) with long gaps where GPU sits idle waiting on NCCL ops. nvprof shows many short kernels interleaved and large NCCL launch overhead.

maya: ```
NCCL allReduce size=9216 bytes peer=7 start=0x7fb...
NCCL coll time: 2.1ms wait_for_launch: 0.9ms sync_overhead: 0.8ms
kernel: fused_attention_backward small-seq kernel chosen: cudaKernel_v2 (1.2ms)
```

sasha: interesting — kernel autoswitch might be preferring a kernel optimized for small seqs that has worse stream concurrency. did we change kernel selection thresholds recently?

ciara: also seeing KV cache churn in the same run. KVCACHE: evictions=4.2k, misses spike during warmup. if prefix caching yields many tiny kv packets, that increases all-reduce count.

maya: good call. I compared two runs: with kvcache disabled throughput is back to baseline. with kvcache enabled, we flood all-reduce with ~8-12KB msgs.

perf-bot: perf-summary: nightly/2026-03-17 03:12: p99_latency +16%, tokens/s -14%, NCCL short-msg count +410%

cheng: hypothesis: small message sizes push NCCL ring into high per-coll overhead. ring is O(msg_count) and does poorly on many tiny calls. tree/allgather variants sometimes batch differently (fewer launches). maybe runtime should switch to tree for <16KB?

liam: also consider coalescing window. current batching window is 2ms. for TP pipeline micro-batches we're seeing many mini-colls inside the window. increasing to 4-6ms might coalesce more tokens and reduce all-reduce frequency. but watch latency SLO.

sasha: kernel selection + batching + kvcache fragmentation = three-way interaction. proposal: add guardrail: if kvcache enabled and avg_msg_size < 16KB then 1) temporarily increase coalesce window, 2) prefer tree all-reduce implementation, 3) force kernel variant with better stream overlap.

ciara: we should measure memory pressure tradeoffs. coalescing will increase CPU buffering and maybe push more into KV memory.

maya: quick repro script I used (small model sequence-lengths):
```bash
# repro harness
python run_tp_perf.py --model 2B --tp 8 --seq 32 --batch 1 --kvcache on --repeat 500
# capture traces: export PROFILER=nvtx && ./run...
```

liam: I'll run with tree-enabled fallback (runtime flag) and bump coalesce to 5ms on my rig. will post traces.

perf-bot: trace-link: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/2323456789 (flame + nccl-events)

cheng: if tree fallback reduces coll count but increases per-coll latency, need to quantify token/sec. target is TOKEN_S / GPU >= baseline. set an A/B test on nightly.

maya: plan: 1) liam run tree-fallback + coalesce=5ms (today) 2) sasha add kernel-variant gating by kvcache msg_size (next PR) 3) ciara run memory + kvcache telemetry to see effect on evictions 4) cheng run A/B on nightly to compare token/s and p99.

liam: started run now. ETA ~12m. posting logs when done. :eyes:

sasha: I'll draft the runtime config change - small guard rails only behind a runtime flag. also add unit tests for selection logic.

ciara: I'll attach kvcache histograms after run.

maya: thanks. tagging @oncall if we see this in prod. for now mark as P2 perf regression.

liam: update - tree fallback cut NCCL short-coll count by ~70% and tokens/s up ~9% vs kvcache-on baseline. p99 still slightly worse than kvcache-off. attaching quick diff.

maya: promising. sounds like combined approach needed. thanks team. :thumbsup:
